points.description: Takes a clear position on the essay's topic and states it so the reader can identify it. Equivalent wording earns the mark. A position that is vague, missing or changes during the essay earns no credit here.

Develops the position with reasoning and supporting evidence. Stronger development means more well-reasoned, specific and convincing support. Thin, uneven or unsupported argument earns less. Any valid supporting reasons or examples are acceptable.

Organises the essay coherently, with a logical sequence of ideas and paragraphs that support the position. Equivalent structures, such as a clear introduction, body and conclusion, earn the mark. Lapses in organisation reduce credit.

Uses precise language with few errors in grammar, spelling and punctuation. Errors that do not obstruct meaning are penalised in proportion to their frequency. Errors that obstruct meaning earn no credit here.

rubric.notes: The model answer is a holistic six-band scale, so the four marks-bearing ideas (position, development, organisation, language) are each worth 1.5 and the total is 6. Full credit means a clear, well-developed, well-organised essay with almost no errors (band 5 to 6); partial credit follows the band descriptors, with thin development, lapses in organisation or frequent errors reducing marks; no credit means no clear position and errors that obstruct meaning (band 1). Equivalent wording and alternative valid arguments earn full marks.
